summary: You take the core seminars (including both quarters of TAPS 301), the TAPS workshops, the production course and five elective graduate seminars (TAPS 200-399, at least 20 units), each for a letter grade where offered, toward 135 units, of which at most 6 can be TAPS 390 Directed Reading. The three examinations, the repertory performance project, candidacy, the prospectus, the oral exam, the dissertation and the language requirement are checked by hand.

P0aDMTSQ.why: "Stanford Ph.D. students must complete a minimum of 135 units of graduate courses and seminars in support of the degree." The program total, now program.unitsMin; the rest is an advising chart.

oplqduOb.why: TAPS 301 "is a two-quarter required course in which students enroll for two units in autumn and two units in winter" (the Examinations text names it: "TAPS 301 World Theater History. This is a two-quarter required course"). A second slot for the second quarter. Grading: "Students are expected to enroll in all required courses for a letter grade unless that option is not available."

BC86fblc.why: "At least five additional graduate seminars (for a minimum total of 20 units) are required within the Department of Theater and Performance Studies ... students must take five TAPS classes at the 200- or 300-level, such as the following seminars". The 20 units were stored as a floor on the whole block. The block note caps Directed Reading: "Students can take up to 6 units of TAPS 390 Directed Reading to count towards the 135 units". Grading: "Students are expected to enroll in all required courses for a letter grade unless that option is not available."

vvWGjGG8.why: "Students must successfully complete three examinations (comprehensive, qualifying, and department oral) by the end of the third year in the program."

dhhYe2xN.why: "Each student will undertake the production of a substantial creative project as one of the departmental milestones for the second year." Its course, TAPS 376, is already a required workshop.

TWd6HbUN.why: "Students must demonstrate reading knowledge of one foreign language" by an ETS score, a department reading examination, or "A grade of B or higher in a 100-level or higher foreign language course at Stanford". Any language, so a person checks it.
